name: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana
nodalDept: Department of Health and Family Welfare
briefDescription: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY gives eligible poor and vulnerable families cashless health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year at empanelled hospitals.
descriptionMd: Ayushman Bharat – Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB PM-JAY) is the world's largest health-assurance scheme, run by the Department of Health & Family Welfare. It provides eligible low-income families in both rural and urban areas with **cashless hospital cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year**, so that a medical emergency does not push a family into debt. Care is delivered at empanelled public and private hospitals across the country.
benefitsMd:
- **Cashless cover of up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year** for hospitalisation.
- Covers the full treatment chain — consultation, medicines, diagnostics, surgery, ICU, implants, room and food.
- Includes **3 days of pre-hospitalisation** and **15 days of post-hospitalisation** expenses.
- Covers complications that arise during treatment.
- **Pre-existing conditions are covered from day one.**
- **No cap on family size, age or gender** — every eligible member is covered.
eligibilityMd:
Eligibility is based on the deprivation and occupational categories of the SECC database, so there is **no enrolment fee or age limit**.

In **rural areas**, families qualify if they fall under the SECC deprivation criteria, along with automatic inclusion for the most vulnerable — the destitute or those surviving on alms, manual scavenger households, primitive tribal groups, and legally released bonded labourers. Eligible **urban** households are identified through their occupational category. You can check your eligibility on the PM-JAY portal or at any empanelled hospital.
exclusionsMd: 1. Those who own a two, three, or four-wheeler or a motorized fishing boat. 1. Those who own mechanized farming equipment. 1. Those who have Kisan cards with a credit limit of ₹50,000/-. 1. Those employed by the government. 1. Those who work in government-managed non-agricultural enterprises. 1. Those earning a monthly income above ₹10,000/-. 1. Those owning refrigerators and landlines. 1. Those with decent, solidly built houses. 1. Those owning 5 acres or more of agricultural land.
applicationMd:
There is no separate online application — identification is done with help from an **Arogya Mitra** at any empanelled hospital or Common Service Centre (CSC):

**Step 1:** Submit your PM letter / RSBY URN / ration card number / mobile number. The operator searches the beneficiary list using these details.
**Step 2:** The operator searches the BIS application against the SECC, RSBY and state health-scheme databases.
**Step 3:** **Individual identification** — your Aadhaar or government ID and ration card (or family ID) are verified and scanned.
**Step 4:** **Family identification** — family records are confirmed through the ration card, and the documents are uploaded and submitted for approval.
**Step 5:** The trust or insurance company **approves or recommends rejection**; rejections are finally decided by the State Health Agency (SHA).
**Step 6:** Once approved, your **e-card is issued** and you can avail cashless treatment.
